messages.subject: Removal of under-represented SNPs
messages.body_plain: We are doing QTL analysis in diversity outbred mice and have a question regarding removing rare SNP alleles. We have a lower 'n' than ideal but cannot repeat the experiment to add more. In our analysis we have some QTLs with massive effects that aren't significant, which we think is due to one mouse having a particularly low or high phenotype and being the only sample to have the specific allele at that locus. It was recommended to us that we could delete the rare SNPs but we are unsure how. Has anyone done this or know how? Thank you!

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] Removal of under-represented SNPs
messages.body_plain:
You could remove a set of SNPs by name using the function drop_markers(). But I don't think this is the cause of the problem.

You could calculate the SNP allele frequencies like this:

  g <- do.call("cbind", mycross$geno)
  pA <- (colSums(g==1) + 0.5*colSums(g==2)) / colSums(g != 0)

Make a histogram:

  hist(pA, breaks=200)

Omit markers where the allele frequency is < 0.05 or > 0.95.

  todrop <- names(pA)[pA < 0.05 | pA > 0.95]
  mycross_sub <- drop_markers(mycross, todrop)

But I don't think the genotype probabilities are much affected by the presence of rare SNPs, and so I don't think your results, and the fact that you have some messed up estimated QTL effects, will much change.

Rather, I think the problem is due to particular diplotypes or haplotypes being essentially absent in a region. So the genotype probabilities or allele dosages will have a column that is basically all 0, but it won't be ~quite~ 0 due to round off error. We need to omit such columns before fitting the regression, but when the values are exactly 0, the algorithm doesn't handle it well.

You can try using the function clean_genoprob() to threshold small probabilities to 0. It sort of works, but not perfectly. I've not yet found a great solution to this.

  my_genoprob <- clean_genoprob(my_genoprob)

karl
